name: Nimrod
overview: Nimrod is a male figure noted in Scripture as the son of Cush and described as a mighty hunter before the LORD. His identity is primarily grounded in his unique attribute as a powerful hunter, highlighting his strength and prominence in the early post-Flood generations. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or other personal details beyond these points.
namesAndTitles: The name Nimrod is a proper name that may mean 'to rebel' or 'the Arrow, the mighty hero.' This suggests a character known for strength and possibly defiance, though the biblical text simply presents the name without explicit divine origin or additional titles.
familyAndRelationships: Nimrod is identified in Scripture as the son of Cush. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are recorded in the biblical text provided. Therefore, his lineage is directly traced to Cush alone.
scriptureSignificance: Nimrod's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his reputation as a mighty hunter before the LORD, indicating a figure of notable power and influence in the early generations after the Flood. His mention as Cush's son situates him within the genealogical framework that traces the spread of nations. This brief but striking description underscores his role as a prominent leader and warrior in the biblical account.
